Per 4/2 email from Stacy Garcia

This is a “heads-up” email…

 

We are a couple of weeks out from receiving the UMS PDMS PHA from GDMS which will require MRF review by all those on the “TO” line. When you receive the files for review, D422 will have verified that NAVSEA comments were incorporated as adjudicated in the [NAVSEA approval letter|https://ora.ebnet.gdeb.com:4443/pls/APPL/display.document_file?file_id=130006269803203], and we will be ready to submit for information and HIF acknowledgement.

 

As with the C2S PHA submittal for info, the EB MRF review has been allotted for one week, expected to begin Monday, April 20 with planned distribution to NAVSEA on Friday, April 24. Therefore, we will be looking for review/signature from {+}Monday, April 20 through Thursday, April 23{+}. I know it’s a few weeks out, but if you foresee any challenge with meeting this ECD, please let me know. As a reminder, this step is verbatim comment incorporation, so unless there are NAVSEA comments that were not adequately incorporated, we are not able to take comments regarding items outside of the NAVSEA comments linked above.

 

I will provide updates as we move through the next two weeks and look to receive the final files from GDMS. Thank you!

column10: Welcome to the SSWUMS Team space, led by Meridith K (Product Owner). This space includes D440 and D454 resources, as well as Sprint and Kanban work.
column49:
Per 1/16/2026 email, forwarded by Adam White, from Ethan Teodosio.

The SSW FOCS TI-24 ICD Revision A was posted yesterday, 1/14/26. Please review and provide comments by 3/2/2026 and concurrence/sign-off by 05/01/2026.

This is a brand-new ICD for the SSW boat, and as a result, a full review is required by each subsystem to confirm that all changes have been incorporated. Commitments will be taken out against all subsystems to provide signature by 05/01/2026 and the commitment numbers will be provided during the next status update email.

If you are not the correct POC, email me so we can make the correction on the commitment.

*+ACCESS TO THE ICD:+*

PI Web can be found at [https://www.gdeb.com/contracts/nssn_c3i/]. Please apply for an account if you have not done so yet.

If assistance is required with accessing the site, please email [pi_web@gdeb.com|mailto:pi_web@gdeb.com].

*+HOW TO REVIEW:+*

When reviewing, please provide comments in the form of redlines against the ICD itself, changing whichever cells need adjustment and highlighting BOTH the changed cells AND the wiremarker column (COLUMN B). For ease of reviewing, subsystems can filter the SYSTEM SEARCH column (AR) by their subsystem name. After filtering the ICD this way, proceed to check each wiremarker including the LINK FUNCTION and REMARKS.

Throughout the document are cells labeled "TBD" which is used to indicate that information has not yet been provided by the affiliated subsystem. TBD cells highlighted *+ORANGE+*  were required to be provided during the initial GFI drops and were missed. This information is needed *urgently* to support system design reviews starting in February and needs to be prioritized.

In the event that you have further questions on how to perform a review of the FOCS ICD, please do not hesitate to reach out to me or Lance Derosiers.

Check through our existing documentation to verify the usage, or lack thereof, of rare earth materials on GDMS HW deliverables. Requested due date is 11/4. Requester is Dave Kapusta via [~awhite3] 
----
Original email - COMPANY SENSITIVE:

EB has requested we provide a list of all rare earth element based magnets used on submarines.  I am looking for information for every CFE system / subsystem, negative responses are required.

Rare earth magnets are composed of elements from the rare earth group of the periodic table. The two most likely that come up in most google searches are:
 * Neodymium Magnets (NdFeB):   Made from alloys of iron, boron, and neodymium, these magnets are commonly used types of rare earth magnets.
 * Samarium-Cobalt Magnets (SmCo):   Made from the alloy of cobalt and samarium, they are not that common compared to neodymium magnets. However, they come with specific advantages for certain applications.

Two actions requested to support:
 # Need a list of any engineered component that uses a large quantity of rare earth element magnets *+ASAP+*

o   Large quantity defined as more than a few pounds per component (yes, I know how subjective this is)
 # Please have your engineering teams complete the spreadsheet by next Tuesday COB, *+11/4.+*

I have attached the spreadsheet for your teams to fill out.  Consider for purposes of this drill that COTS items such as hard drives, speakers, headphones, fans, etc. should all be listed, but at this time we do not need to determine the weight of magnet per component.  For custom engineered components, please fill out all lines on the spreadsheet.

You do not need to list any GFE hardware which uses rare earth element magnets.  That will be handled separately.

Please reach out directly if you have any questions.  This ask from corporate did not come with a lot of background information, so we are learning as we go.

Description of VIR in SPARS:

General Dynamics is submitting the following VIR for confirmation of direction and concurrence of assumed responsibility.

Reference EB-6101 and EB-6501
EB-6101 [SYS-4.6.5-5] states, in part "Where Class 1 or Class 2 ESDS parts or assemblies are used, the equipment design shall [SYS-4.6.5-6] include protective circuitry that ensures all external electrical inputs, outputs and interface connection points exhibit MIL-STD-1686B Class 3 ESD voltage sensitivities (4,000 to 15,999 Volts) or are not ESD sensitive (sensitivity >16,000 Volts)."

EB-6101 references MIL-STD-1686B is the governing document for compliance, MIL-STD-1686B provides direction to utilize MIL-STD-883 in appendix A as guidance for testing electronic assemblies. MIL-STD-883 provides two critical pieces of information, a process, and a waveform that is utilized for destructive type purposes to ensure the unit under test is immune or protected at the desired Electrostatic discharge class.

We have received guidance from the EB ESD team to utilize EB-6501, which utilizes an IEC 61000-4-2 waveform, instead of the MIL-STD-883 waveform directed by the EB-6101 to MIL-STD-1686B to Mil-STD-883 traceability.

GDMS is requesting confirmation that testing to EB-6501 (and the IEC 61000-4-2 waveform) can be utilized as OQE to meeting EB-6101 SYS-4.6.5-5.
